messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: High 5xx rate observed for inference-gateway in us-west-2. Alert: gateway.5xx_rate > 5% for 3m. link: https://pager.redwood.company/alerts/3952
jun (oncall): on it. grabbing dashboards now.
maria: seeing a sharp jump in 502s and some 504s starting ~10:12 UTC. latency p50 normal but p95 skyrockets.
alex: I can confirm a spike across both edge and regional gateways in us-west-2. Backend responses show many upstream connection resets.
jun (oncall): any deploys in the last 30m?
ben: no user deploys logged. infra deploy bot shows none. recent config change: autoscaling policy tweak at 09:50 but that was for Dedicated pools, not gateway.
kim: pulling logs. gateway-proxy logs show a pattern: "upstream reset" followed by "dial tcp: i/o timeout". suspecting egress NAT or transient infra saturation. snippet:
```
proxy[pid=4521] ERROR upstream: dial tcp 10.34.9.21:443: i/o timeout
proxy[pid=4521] WARN upstream: connection reset by peer
```
jun (oncall): check egress path to mlworkers and model-serving pools. can someone run traceroute and curl health endpoints?
maria: curl from a gateway host to mlworker health /health returns 200 but high connection latency and intermittent timeouts:
```
$ time curl -sS http://10.34.9.21:8080/health -m 5 -o /dev/null
real 5.01s
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 5001 milliseconds
```
alex: looking at NAT gateway metrics in us-west-2, SNAT conn tracking is near capacity on a subset of nodes. Connection churn high. metric link: https://metrics.redwood.company/d/egress/nat-usw2
sre-bot: Runbook step 2: If conntrack exhaustion suspected, consider failover to secondary egress pool or enable regional fallback routing.
jun (oncall): prioritize quick mitigation: 1) shift external outgoing traffic to backup egress pool, 2) enable routing fallback for new requests to eu-west-1 while preserving sticky sessions if possible. any risks?
kim: two risks: session-affinity (KV cache) and increased latency for users in region. need to ensure model-context KV cache isn't invalidated on reroute.
ben: can do a staged traffic steer at the edge proxy for non-stickied requests and leave existing stickied connections alone. command ready: `redwoodctl traffic steer --from-region=us-west-2 --to-region=eu-west-1 --percent=20 --route=non-sticky`
jun (oncall): do it. start with 10%. post results.
alex: issuing the steer now.

sre-bot: Action: traffic steer initiated by alex. id: steer-2026-03-15-01. from=us-west-2 to=eu-west-1 percent=10 route=non-sticky

kim: monitoring error rate and customer impact. watch for 502/504 drop.
maria: after the 10% steer, 5xx rate in us-west-2 dropped from 6.2% -> 4.1% within 60s. good sign. overall global p95 latency increased ~120ms for steered traffic.
support-ops: started triage with support. top affected tenants are: tenant_42, tenant_mlkit, tenant_enterprise_7. Support is notifying enterprise customers with elevated errors and collecting request IDs.
product-ops: flagging potential SLO impact for a small subset; will coordinate comms if degradation persists >1h.
jun (oncall): iterative plan: increase steer to 30% in 10m if trend holds, while simultaneously switching some gateway hosts to backup egress pool to relieve conntrack. who owns egress flip?
ben: infra can flip for two subnets now. doing subnet-a first. command: `infractl nat swap --subnet=subnet-a --to=egress-backup`

sre-bot: infra action queued: nat-swap-546. expected tear-through 30s.

alex: nat swap completed for subnet-a. monitoring.

maria: after subnet swap, observed backend connection errors drop on hosts using subnet-a. us-west-2 5xx overall down to 2.6%. good.

kim: proceeding to increase steer to 30% now.

sre-bot: Action: traffic steer updated by kim. id: steer-2026-03-15-01. percent=30

jun (oncall): confirm KV cache behavior for steered requests. is model serving cache shared cross-region?

alex: KV cache is region-local. steered requests will miss cache and incur model warmup/latency but should still succeed. for long-running sessions we won't move active stickies.

maria: long-run mitigation: add more conntrack capacity and fix NAT churn root cause. short-run: keep fallback steer and egress swap until stable.

support-ops: incidents page updated with affected tenants and temporary mitigation links: https://status.redwood.company/incidents/3976543210

product-ops: will prepare a customer note if SLA exposure appears.

jun (oncall): current status update for ops channel: us-west-2 partial outage -> mitigated via egress swap + 30% cross-region steer to eu-west-1. 5xx reduced to <1.5% in last 5m. no data loss. continuing to monitor.

ben: creating follow-up ticket to fully remediate NAT conntrack sizing and add autoscale for connection table. ticket: INFRA-8742. owner: ben. ETA: 2w.

kim: ops actions post-incident: 1) full conntrack capacity audit (owner: kim), 2) add canary for NAT churn (owner: alex), 3) ensure traffic-steer runbook updated (owner: jun).

maria: logging full request_ids for affected window to help support correlate errors -> PR to logging-prod created: https://git.redwood.company/logging/PR-542

support-ops: customer comms draft ready for review. asking product-ops and eng to sign off before 15:30 UTC.

jun (oncall): handing off to day SREs. I'm going offline for sleep. please escalate if recovery regresses above 3% 5xx.

sre-bot: Handoff: oncall change - jun -> alex at 03:00 UTC.

alex: taking over. leaving this channel open, will post a summary + postmortem checklist once everything stable for 2h.

product-ops: flagged for postmortem and SLO review.

support-ops: will follow up with affected customers and provide logs.

maria: final check: steady-state for 30m, no regression in backend latency. marking incident as mitigated but not resolved.

jun (oncall): thanks team. great runbook execution. follow-ups tracked to INFRA-8742, LOG-542, RUNBOOK-211.

alex: closing active pager. will create the incident channel notes and link to this thread.

sre-bot: Incident resolved: mitigation applied. please file incident report within 72h.
